blocks.text: Kennametal India Ltd (KIL) reports on a July-June fiscal year, not April-March: FY25 = July 2024 to June 2025 [F] (AR2025 p.48). We follow the company's convention throughout; the 'Q2 FY23' in this report's title is the September 2022 quarter, which is Q1 FY23 on the company's own calendar [AI]. Our statements data runs only to FY22 (annual) and the September 2022 quarter (quarterly), while share price and shareholding are current to 2026 [F] (NUMBERS). We therefore lean on the FY25 annual report for FY23-FY25 figures [F] (AR2025 p.12). The audited FY26 results (year to June 2026) have been published [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS), but they are not in our evidence set. **No FY26 figure appears in this report, and that gap matters a great deal for any valuation conclusion.**

Data-vintage warning: the trailing multiples and the DCF in our model are built on September 2022 trailing-twelve-month numbers (sales Rs 1,021 cr, EPS Rs 53.28) but use an October 2026 share price (Rs 4,194) [F] (NUMBERS). Every valuation number in this report carries that mismatch [AI].

KIL is a 75%-owned listed subsidiary of Kennametal Inc, USA: Meturit AG, Zug holds 51% and Kennametal Inc holds 24% directly [F] (AR2025 p.102). It has two reportable segments [F] (AR2025 p.177). (1) Hard Metal Products: tungsten-carbide cutting tools (inserts, solid round tools, tooling systems) sold under the Kennametal and WIDIA brands, plus wear-resistant parts and earth-cutting/construction tools [F] (AR2025 p.53). (2) Machining Solutions Group (MSG): special-purpose machines, horizontal machining centres, vertical turning lathes, deep-hole drilling machines and tool-and-cutter grinders under the WIDMA brand [F] (AR2025 p.53). Both segments are made at one plant on Tumkur Road, Bengaluru [F] (AR2025 p.77).

How it makes money: in FY25, 59% of revenue came from manufactured goods (Rs 691.9 cr) and 39% from traded stock-in-trade (Rs 456.0 cr), with services at Rs 21.4 cr [F] (AR2025 p.163). **A large share of what KIL sells is therefore imported from the group and resold** [AI]. Purchases from group companies were Rs 388.5 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.181). Hard metals are a consumable: management puts the split at about 80% consumables and 20% capital equipment [MC] (CALL Jun 2023). The BRSR gives 87% / 13% by turnover [F] (AR2025 p.102).

subsections.title: Bear thesis: the strongest reasons not to own it

items: 1. Valuation is disconnected from every scenario in our DCF. The price of Rs 4,194 compares with bear / base / bull values of Rs 158.8 / 309.6 / 415.9 per share, and the reverse DCF implies 126.4% annual sales growth for five years, against 6.1% in the base case [F] (NUMBERS).

2. Growth is mid-single-digit. Revenue grew 2.1% in FY24 and 6.4% in FY25 [E] (AR2025 p.12); the FY22-FY25 CAGR is about 5.7% [E] (AR2025 p.58). Management's own aspiration was cut from 1.4-1.6x market growth [MC] (CALL Jun 2023) to 1.2-1.3x [MC] (CALL Mar 2024).

3. Margins have not regained the FY22 peak. EBITDA margin was 18% in FY22 [F] (NUMBERS) against about 15.6% in FY24 and 14.7% in FY25 [E] (AR2025 p.135); PBT fell 7.4% in FY25 including the FY24 exceptional item [F] (AR2025 p.27).

4. The parent sets the economics. Group purchases were Rs 388.5 cr (33% of revenue) and group services/recharges Rs 43.2 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.181). Royalty expense more than doubled to Rs 8.5 cr [F] (AR2025 p.166), even though management said the royalty rate was cut to 4% from 4.75% [MC] (CALL Mar 2024).

5. The tax authority disputes KIL's manufacturing margins. The key audit matter covers transfer-pricing demands on 'margin earned on manufacturing activities' [F] (AR2025 p.126). This is an outside party questioning whether the intra-group pricing leaves enough profit in India [AI].

6. MSG profitability collapsed. Segment result fell from Rs 14.4 cr to Rs 5.8 cr in FY25 (margin 9.8% to 3.8%) [E] (AR2025 p.177), on adverse mix, marketing spend and under-absorption [MC] (AR2025 p.45).
7. Working capital is heavy. Inventory of Rs 294.9 cr is 30.5% of total assets [E] (AR2025 p.133), and the cash conversion cycle is about 160-170 days [E] (AR2025 p.133, p.135); [F] (NUMBERS).

8. Liquidity is thin and institutional sponsorship is narrowing. FIIs fell from 0.93% to 0.23% between June 2025 and June 2026 [F] (NUMBERS); 88.49% of shares sit in 8 holdings [F] (AR2025 p.76); monthly BSE volume in FY25 ranged from 47,694 to 158,911 shares [F] (AR2025 p.75).

9. Disclosure is sparse. There is no capacity, utilisation, order book, end-market split, export margin or investor presentation, and management calls this 'competitive intelligence' or 'price sensitive' [MC] (CALL Jun 2023), (CALL May 2023).
10. Single-site concentration: one plant at Tumkur Road, Bengaluru, and 100% imported tungsten [F] (AR2025 p.102); [MC] (CALL Mar 2023).

blocks.text: [AI] The consensus framing, as in the board notes, is a high-quality MNC consumables franchise with pricing power [AI] (BOARD). Our variant view: the franchise is real, but the listed entity is closer to a regulated profit-centre of its parent than an independent compounder. About a third of revenue is resold group product [E] (AR2025 p.163, p.181); fundamental R&D, grades and pricing sit abroad [MC] (CALL Mar 2023); and the transfer-pricing envelope, now contested by the tax authority, limits how far margins can rise [F] (AR2025 p.126). Audited FY23-FY25 results track our base DCF closely. The sevenfold move from Rs 1,947 (FY25 low) [F] (AR2025 p.75) to a 52-week high of Rs 5,136 [F] (NUMBERS) is not explained by anything in our evidence set. Either FY26 contained a step-change we cannot see, or the price reflects scarcity, flows and expectations rather than disclosed fundamentals.

[AI] The business is old (Widia heritage, 60 AGMs). What is recent is the operating base: the insert building (late 2022), the MSG export push to China and then its reversal, the new royalty terms (April 2024), and an almost entirely refreshed board (four changes in FY25) [F] (AR2025 p.36). items: Step 1, raw material: tungsten carbide/APT and cobalt, 100% imported because India has no tungsten mine [MC] (CALL Mar 2023); basic powders come from a third party and some grade powders from group entities [MC] (CALL Mar 2023).
Step 2, powder processing: KIL runs its own powder manufacturing [MC] (CALL Mar 2023) and lists in-house powder manufacturing as import substitution in its R&D work [F] (AR2025 p.90).
Step 3, pressing, sintering, grinding, coating (CVD/PVD), brazing: sintering cycles and CVD coatings were transferred from Kennametal Inc in 2017-2025 [F] (AR2025 p.90).

Step 4, traded high-end products: low-volume, high-end items are imported from group plants (mainly USA/Germany) and resold [MC] (CALL Mar 2024); stock-in-trade sales were Rs 456.0 cr in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.163).
Step 5, distribution: more than 225-240 channel partners handle 80-87% of hard-metal sales [MC] (CALL Jun 2023), (CALL Mar 2024).
Step 6, application engineering: trials, prove-outs and training through the Kennametal Knowledge Center (47 events, 1,081 attendees in FY25) [F] (AR2025 p.57).
MSG: design, machine building, commissioning and after-service in-house [MC] (AR2025 p.37); domestic MSG sales are direct, export sales go through channel partners [MC] (CALL Mar 2024).

blocks.text: [AI] Value accrues where the product proves a lower cost per component in the customer's process. Management describes this as 'top of the pyramid applications' [MC] (CALL Mar 2023). For KIL the capture is split. On manufactured goods KIL keeps the manufacturing margin, less a royalty of about 4% on IP-protected products [MC] (CALL Mar 2024). On traded goods transfer-pricing rules leave a 'limited distributor margin' [MC] (CALL Mar 2023). Hard metals earned a 16.1% segment margin in FY25; MSG earned 3.8% [E] (AR2025 p.177). Moving mix towards local manufacture is the main margin lever: 'the more we produce domestically ... we have ability to manage our profitability' [MC] (CALL May 2023).

Subcontracting charges were Rs 41.7 cr in FY25 (Rs 36.8 cr in FY24) [F] (AR2025 p.166). Gross block was Rs 530.0 cr against FY25 revenue of Rs 1,170.3 cr, about 2.2x revenue to gross block [E] (AR2025 p.133). Capex was 2.7% of revenue in both FY24 and FY25 [E] (AR2025 p.138). Most production machinery is imported, with lead times of up to about 10 months [MC] (CALL May 2023). [AI] This is moderately capital-intensive manufacturing combined with an asset-light trading layer; the blended profile is mid-intensity.

subsections.title: What is known about the current year

blocks.text: The latest quarter in our statements data is September 2022: sales Rs 267 cr (+12.2% YoY), EBITDA Rs 47 cr (18%), PAT Rs 32 cr at a 19% tax rate [F] (NUMBERS). For FY26 the annual report said only that the year was 'expected to grow at the same pace as the last year' and that the company 'remains cautious in its outlook' [MC] (AR2025 p.55). FY26 results exist [F] (ANNOUNCEMENTS) but are not in our evidence. No order backlog for FY26 is disclosed. Customer advances of Rs 33.7 cr at June 2025 (Rs 22.9 cr a year earlier) [F] (AR2025 p.164) are the only quantified indicator of deferred machine revenue.

[AI] Mostly mix and parent allocation, not a KIL export strategy. Hard-metal exports go only to group companies; KIL does not sell tools directly to foreign customers [MC] (CALL Mar 2023), (CALL Mar 2024). Volumes depend on the parent's 'capacity allocation ... best cost position' [MC] (CALL Mar 2023). Related-party revenue was Rs 155.9 cr [F] (AR2025 p.180), about 85% of total exports [E]. KIL's own export strategy covers only MSG machines (China, Southeast Asia, Middle East), and management called it 'slow' and 'nothing yet concrete' [MC] (CALL Jun 2023), (CALL Mar 2024).

items: Currency: foreign exchange used was Rs 543.9 cr against Rs 192.3 cr earned in FY25 [F] (AR2025 p.91). [AI] Rupee weakness reaches KIL mainly through repricing of rupee transfer prices, which is invisible in the hedging disclosure. KIL had no derivatives [F] (AR2025 p.128).

Tariffs: the Chairman flagged 'a steep tariff hike on Indian goods by the U.S.' as a challenge for coming quarters [MC] (AR2025 p.35); the exact date is not given in our documents. US-bound revenue was Rs 69.0 cr (5.9%), almost all intercompany hard metals [F] (AR2025 p.178).
China: MSG exposure to China fell to Rs 20.2 cr [F] (AR2025 p.178); recovery has been 'L' shaped [MC] (CALL Mar 2024).

Single location: one plant and five offices, all in India [F] (AR2025 p.102). There is no disclosed business-continuity plan or insurance limit beyond 'sufficient insurance coverage' [MC] (AR2025 p.50).
